summary.headline: Caliber Mining H1 FY27 normalized revenue up 59.5% to INR992 crore; Q2 overburden removal up 109% YoY despite monsoon.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 was seasonally weak, but overburden removal rose 109% YoY to 33 million cubic metres and coal extraction rose 78% to 0.76 million tonnes. Normalized revenue (excluding diesel pass-through) grew more than 90% YoY in Q2, and normalized EBITDA margin was 16.60% versus 12.14% a year earlier. Management reiterated FY27 guidance of 45%+ revenue growth and 35%+ EBITDA and PAT growth, and targets about 60 million cubic metres of overburden removal in each of Q3 and Q4. Post-IPO net worth rose to INR1,148.42 crore and net debt-to-equity fell to 0.95x from 1.48x.

segments.name: Coal mining services (overburden removal and coal extraction)
segments.commentary: Contributed 88% of Q2 FY27 revenue. H1 FY27 overburden removal was 76.49 million cubic metres vs 44.40 million (up 72%); H1 coal extraction grew 41%.

segments.name: Logistics
segments.commentary: Contributed 10% of Q2 FY27 revenue. Loaded 9.83 million tonnes of coal in H1 FY27 (up 50%) and transported 2.44 million metric tonnes in Q2 FY27 (up 42%).

segments.name: Other ancillary services
segments.commentary: Balance of Q2 FY27 revenue (about 2%), not separately quantified.

guidance_outlook: FY27 guidance reiterated: revenue growth of 45%+ YoY, and EBITDA and PAT growth of 35%+ YoY.
Q3 and Q4 overburden removal target of about 60 million cubic metres per quarter; management said H2 revenue typically about 1.5x H1.
Q2 PAT was about INR157 crore base; management indicated H2 PAT of approximately INR205-210 crore.
October FY27: overburden removal above 180 million cubic metres (stated as 180 million cubic metre quantity) and about 6.4-6.5 lakh tonnes of coal.
Next-year (FY28) fleet, capex and tentative numbers to be given with Q3 FY27 results in December 2026.
Capex now mostly complete for current order book; further capex only if new contracts are won or customers demand 105-120% of contracted volumes.
risks_watch: Q2 is seasonally weak; H2 delivery of the 60 million cubic metre quarterly target depends on no major disruptions.
Jayant OC1 is in an extension period; INR63 crore of work is still pending per the presentation, and the customer granted an extension at existing rates.
Management did not quantify AI productivity gains (Pulse 1 and Pulse 2 systems, Pulse 2 in beta from November 1).
Working-capital and debt impact of any MDO win is undisclosed; MDO bids are still in discussions with private players.
The FY28 fleet and guidance will be given only in December 2026 with Q3 results.
Net loss of INR7.51 crore in Q2 remains, with depreciation and finance costs rising with fleet expansion.
Diesel pass-through is retrospective from March 24; the change in clause from retail to bulk diesel price has been described only qualitatively.
Reported Q2 ~ revenue and margins include diesel pass-through, so reported EBITDA margins are lower than normalized figures.
summary.management_tone: Confident and promotional. Management was emphatic on reiterating FY27 guidance and H2 volume targets. It was evasive on MDO economics, AI quantification, tender win rates, and pricing in new bids, citing competitive sensitivity or lack of contracts.
key_quotes: It has been the best H1 and quarter 2 results in the history of Caliber Mining.
We are targeting about 60 million cubic meter of overburden removal in each quarter 3 and quarter 4.
Post-IPO, now it is a different ball game.
Otherwise, we have done all our capex maximum of H2 also in H1.

qa_highlights.question: Why did EBITDA margin fall despite strong revenue growth, and why would H2 margins improve?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q2 FY26 margin was 12.14% on INR228 crore revenue and Q2 FY27 revenue rose 92% to INR441 crore with margin up 446 bps; H2 benefits from no monsoon and from 100% diesel pass-through, with Q3 and Q4 at about 1.5x H1 revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Can you guide on EBITDA margin and PAT for H2 FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated H2 PAT of approximately INR205-210 crore (about 35% growth on the INR157 crore base) and said EBITDA is also expected to grow 35%+ without giving a margin figure.

qa_highlights.question: How will the order book be executed and is there capex for the rest of the year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said capacity for current orders is fully planned and execution has started; capex for 100% of contracted volume is complete, and further capex is needed only for customer requests of 105-120% or new contract wins.

qa_highlights.question: Of the INR11,000 crore tenders, how many bids are L1 and are MDO bids in progress?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it cannot expect to win all tenders; post-IPO liquidity lets it bid more broadly. The INR11,000 crore is non-MDO; MDO opportunities are in discussion with private players with no LOA yet.

qa_highlights.question: Why is INR63 crore of work pending at Jayant OC1 past its September 2026 completion date?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the customer granted an extension at existing rates and conditions because the customer wanted uninterrupted coal and had extra work area available.

qa_highlights.question: How would an MDO win affect working capital, operating cash flow, debt and margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to quantify, saying impact depends on contract scale (for example INR500 crore vs INR1,000 crore annual revenue) and that it will update via exchange after an LOA.

qa_highlights.question: Can AI benefits be quantified?
qa_highlights.answer: Management described Pulse 1 (centralised maintenance portal used by 200+ people) and Pulse 2 (beta from November 1), but declined to quantify productivity gains and invited the analyst to visit Nagpur and Chandrapur.

capex_capacity: H1 FY27 capex of INR584.88 crore, deployed to mobilise three new contracts (Dhoptala II, Dudhichua II, Jayant II) and to meet customer demand beyond targeted volumes.
Fleet stood at 2,226 units vs 2,033 as at June 30; management said it would add fleet beyond 2,226 only if new work is awarded.
Capex for the current order book is essentially complete; management said H2 capex is already pulled forward into H1.
Pre-capex under way for customers seeking 105%, 110% and higher of contracted volumes; further major capex only if new contracts are added in H2.
Out of INR377.16 crore net IPO proceeds, INR371 crore utilised per objects of the issue with no deviation.
FY28 fleet size, capex and tentative numbers to be given with Q3 FY27 results in December 2026.
demand_pricing: Order book covers nine sites with average tenure of about 2.5 years; approximately INR4,000+ crore of orders won in H1 FY27.
Net new tenders of INR11,000+ crore submitted (non-MDO), results awaited; a further INR4,000+ crore of tenders being evaluated for bidding within about 10 days.
MDO opportunities being explored with private players; no MDO bids confirmed as LOA yet.
Pricing: average LOA price is INR89-92 with 100% diesel pass-through; management said crude price moves of INR80-120 do not affect margin guidance.
Diesel pass-through billed in the same month for some customers and 15-day or monthly billing for others; retrospective from March 24.
Management cited power demand projection of 6.8% a year to FY30 with coal at 60% of the mix; customers are asking for 100%+ of contracted volumes.
Management declined to comment on tender pricing versus earlier bids, citing competitive sensitivity.

adds.what: Fleet of 2,226 units (up from 2,033 at June 30); further fleet additions only if new work is awarded
Pre-capex for customers seeking 105-110%+ of contracted volumes (mobilisation of Dhoptala II, Dudhichua II, Jayant II contracts)

growth.why: FY27 guidance of 45%+ revenue and 35%+ EBITDA/PAT growth is reiterated, backed by a nine-site order book (~2.5-year average tenure), INR4,000+ crore of H1 orders, and a fleet of 2,226 units with H1 capex of INR584.88 crore; Q3/Q4 overburden target of ~60 Mcm per quarter and H2 revenue guided at ~1.5x H1, though no explicit FY27 capacity timeline beyond current fleet was given.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q2 normalized EBITDA margin rose to 16.60% from 12.14% YoY, H2 benefits from no monsoon and 100% diesel pass-through, and management reiterated 35%+ EBITDA growth (no margin figure given).

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.when: FY28, with Q3 FY27 results in Dec 2026
rows.why: Fleet is 2,226 units (up from 2,033 at June 30) and further fleet is added only if new work is awarded; INR4,000+ crore of orders won in H1 and INR11,000+ crore of non-MDO tenders pending, so timing depends on wins.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management targets about 60 million cubic metres of overburden removal per quarter in Q3 and Q4 (Q2 was 33 Mcm), and H2 revenue is guided at about 1.5x H1 on a nine-site order book with ~2.5-year average tenure.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex for the current order book is essentially complete (H1 capex INR584.88 crore), so further major capex depends on new contract wins or customers demanding 105-120% of contracted volumes, with pre-capex already under way.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management only reiterated FY27 guidance of 45%+ revenue growth and 35%+ EBITDA and PAT growth; no raise was signalled, and H1 normalized revenue is already up 59.5% against that guide.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: H2 delivery of 60 Mcm per quarter depends on no major disruptions after a seasonally weak Q2 (down 21% QoQ), and INR63 crore of Jayant OC1 work is past its September 2026 completion date under an extension.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: No new products, brands or models were discussed; AI tools Pulse 1 and Pulse 2 are internal systems, with Pulse 2 in beta from November 1.

rows.label: Non-MDO tender wins (INR11,000+ crore submitted)
rows.why: INR11,000+ crore of non-MDO tenders are awaiting results and a further INR4,000+ crore is being evaluated, after INR4,000+ crore of orders were won in H1 FY27, though management said it cannot expect to win all tenders.

rows.label: MDO contracts with private players
rows.why: MDO opportunities are being explored with private players with no LOA yet, and management declined to quantify working-capital, debt or margin impact (examples cited: INR500-1,000 crore annual revenue).

rows.label: AI productivity gains (Pulse 1 and Pulse 2)
rows.why: Pulse 1 is in use by 200+ people and Pulse 2 is in beta from November 1, but management declined to quantify productivity gains, so the margin benefit is not yet evidenced.

tone.note: Management was confident in reiterating FY27 guidance, H2 overburden targets of about 60 Mcm per quarter and H2 PAT of INR205-210 crore, but was evasive on MDO economics, AI quantification, tender win rates and new bid pricing; analysts pressed on margins, the Jayant OC1 delay and tender conversion.
